about: Source of truth for docs/EXPERIMENT_REGISTRY.md (generated by scripts/build_registry_doc.py). Checked by tests/test_repo_hygiene.py. Statements about v1 scripts come from the 2026-11-21 audit (docs/REPOSITORY_AUDIT.md and its appendices). Entries marked FIXED refer to docs/v1/DEFECT_FIXES.md.

tiers.v1-confirmatory: The corrected, leak-free v1 protocol. Code-derived numbers are authoritative; see COMPUTATIONAL_ERRATUM.md for how they relate to the dissertation text.
tiers.v2-validation: Post-dissertation tests of the v1 claims, run on the authorized data with committed, hash-locked records.
tiers.public-replication: Run on public data. Anyone can repeat it.
tiers.exploratory: Hypothesis-generating. Not corrected for the analyses tried, or superseded, as each entry says.
tiers.archived: Legacy v1 chapter analyses kept for provenance. Known leakage, legacy input or uncorrected statistics. Descriptive only.
tiers.illustrative: Synthetic-data demonstrations and presentation figures. They establish no empirical claim about EEG.

experiments.title: v1 confirmatory classification (corrected protocol)
experiments.question: Does the BSC6 / SRP-64 reservoir code separate affective conditions on held-out participants, and how does it compare with raw ERP bins and conventional features?
experiments.model: N=256, beta=0.05, theta=0.5, dense uniform W_rec scaled to spectral radius 0.9, one scalar input per electrode; a different reservoir per electrode (seed 42 + 17 x channel); full 256-sample epoch in six 42-sample bins (last 4 samples dropped); fixed SparseRandomProjection 1536 to 64, seed 20240517
experiments.protocol: 5 repeats x 5-fold StratifiedGroupKFold by participant; StandardScaler and LogisticRegression(C=1) fitted on training participants only; nothing is fitted before the split
experiments.statistics: participant-cluster percentile bootstrap (2000) over pooled out-of-fold predictions; within-participant permutation test with a ridge stand-in, 100 permutations
experiments.seeds: base seed 0 (three conditions) and 100 (four categories); reservoir 42 with robustness seeds 7 and 99; bootstrap 12345. Deterministic
experiments.metrics: balanced accuracy, paired contrasts, destruction-control drops
experiments.dissertation: Chapter 5. The dissertation reports 60.6% and 53.2%; this committed pipeline produces 64.3% and 54.6%. The gap is reconciled in COMPUTATIONAL_ERRATUM.md, and the dissertation text is not edited.
caveats: The window labels in confirmatory_pipeline.TEMPORAL_WINDOWS ('39-273ms' and so on) do not match the slices, which are quarters of the 0 to 1000 ms epoch.
The permutation p-value 0.0099 is the floor for 100 permutations and uses a different model from the headline. v2 repeated it with the headline model (V2-01).
Input is z-scored per epoch, which invalidates window-specific readings (V2-02).

experiments.title: v2 validation of the measurement chain
experiments.question: Does the deployed reservoir have fading memory, does it add anything over matched non-reservoir controls, and do the v1 controls and statistics hold when done properly?
experiments.model: the v1 LIF operator, one reservoir shared by all electrodes, recurrent gain chosen as the largest grid value passing the label-free fading-memory rule (0.025); BSC6; SRP-64
experiments.protocol: v1 splits and readout (CONF-01), with the readout fitted in the row space of the training matrix; ten stages listed in the runner docstring
experiments.statistics: participant bootstrap (2000); within-participant permutation test with the headline estimator (2000); unbiased two-way variance components with permutation nulls (1000)
experiments.seeds: v1 base seeds; reservoir seeds 42 and 1 to 9; projection seeds 0 to 9; dynamics sample seed 2026. Deterministic: a replay of 19 values on fresh encodings equals the record (V2-06)
experiments.metrics: balanced accuracy, paired contrasts, fading-memory measurements, variance fractions
experiments.dissertation: Not in the dissertation. Tests claims made in Chapters 3 to 6. Interpretation in V2_UPGRADE.md.
caveats: The fading-memory rule was written after its author had seen the dynamics sweep. It uses no labels. Gain 0.025 passes at 99% and 0.05 fails at 94%.
The default weight draw (seed 42) is the best of ten; the ten-draw means (65.1% and 55.4%) are the fair summary.
Section 6 of V2_RESULTS.md (windows) is computed on z-scored epochs and cannot be read as timing.
2000 permutations, not the 5000 the review asked for. Zero exceedances at 16.9 and 19.2 null SDs.

experiments.title: Normalization check: per-epoch z-scoring and early-latency decoding
experiments.question: Is above-chance decoding in the first 31 ms after onset produced by v1's per-epoch z-scoring?
experiments.model: no reservoir: 34-electrode scalp pattern in 32 consecutive 31.25 ms bins
experiments.protocol: v1 splits and readout; identical decimation; z-scored versus delivered baseline-corrected input
experiments.dissertation: Bears on every window-specific statement in Chapters 4 and 5 and on the Level-1 statistic r = 0.82.
caveats: Three-condition cohort only.

experiments.title: Pre-specified depression analysis
experiments.question: Do participant-level ERP representations differentiate SCID-5 depression groups (MDE, MDD, Depression_Type, MDD_Recurrent, in that order)?
experiments.model: three representations per participant (LPP mean amplitude, six-bin amplitudes, v2 reservoir code), the three condition vectors concatenated
experiments.protocol: 5 x 5 StratifiedKFold over participants (one row per participant); class-weighted L2 logistic regression fitted in-fold
experiments.statistics: label permutation across participants (1000); Holm correction over the family of 12 tests
experiments.dissertation: Not in the dissertation. Replaces the uncorrected clinical screens of Chapters 6 and 7 with a corrected family.
caveats: Null result: smallest Holm-corrected p = 0.34. Smallest group has 42 participants; this is 'not detected', not 'absent'.
No adjustment for age, sex or medication; demographics are missing for about half the cohort.
The record holds group counts and accuracies only. No participant-level value is written.

experiments.title: Tuned-PCA control for the random-projection comparison
experiments.question: Does SRP-64 still beat fold-local PCA-64 when PCA is left unwhitened and the readout regularization is tuned?
data: cached v2 reservoir codes of both SHAPE cohorts (./v2_cache, derived from restricted data)
experiments.model: v2 headline code; SRP-64 or PCA-64 (basis fitted on outer-training participants, pooled over electrodes); standardized or centered only; C fixed at 1 or tuned
experiments.protocol: v1 outer splits; nested 4-fold participant-grouped CV over C in 1e-4 to 1e2; PCA refitted inside inner folds
experiments.statistics: participant bootstrap (2000) for each variant and paired contrasts
experiments.seeds: v1 base seeds; inner splits base + 1000 + repeat. Deterministic
experiments.dissertation: Retracts the SRP-over-PCA advantage reported in experiments/novel/NOVEL_RESULTS.md (NOV-01) and bears on every PCA-64 row in Chapters 4, 5 and 7.
caveats: The best PCA variant is chosen after seeing its held-out score, which favours PCA on purpose.
The amplitude baselines were tuned afterwards in V2-07.

experiments.title: Reservoir on input without per-epoch z-scoring
experiments.question: With input that never uses a later sample to transform an earlier one, does the early-latency artefact vanish inside the reservoir, and how does the reservoir then compare with its matched control?
experiments.model: v1 LIF operator, shared reservoir; input scaled by each epoch's own pre-stimulus SD, or microvolts divided by one study-wide constant (7.16)
experiments.protocol: as V2-01, plus a 0 to 62 ms window where no picture-content response should exist
experiments.metrics: balanced accuracy, paired contrasts, fading-memory measurements
caveats: The fading-memory rule selects no gain on these inputs, including gain 0: under sustained drive a feedforward LIF neuron keeps its firing phase. The rule was not changed; the feedforward reservoir is used and the outcome recorded.
The reservoir loses to six-bin amplitudes by about 3 points on this input.

experiments.title: Replay check of the v2 record
experiments.question: Is the v2 run deterministic, and does the code in the tree still reproduce the committed record?
experiments.model: as V2-01
experiments.protocol: recomputes the fading-memory sweep and eight representation rows per cohort and compares them with the record for exact equality
experiments.metrics: number of replayed values equal to the record
caveats: Replays 19 of the record's values. Seed sweeps, windows, destruction controls, compressors, variance components and the permutation test are not replayed.

experiments.title: Tuned readout for the amplitude baselines
experiments.question: When every representation gets its own readout regularization, does the ordering of reservoir code, raw ERP and amplitude bins change?
data: cached preprocessed epochs and v2 reservoir codes of both SHAPE cohorts (./v2_cache, derived from restricted data)
experiments.model: v2 headline reservoir code, raw ERP-16, six-bin amplitudes and the per-electrode LPP score, on v1 preprocessing
experiments.protocol: v1 outer splits; nested 4-fold participant-grouped CV over C in 1e-4 to 1e2, with the grid and rule of V2-04; standardized features. Nothing is chosen on outer-test accuracy
experiments.statistics: participant bootstrap (2000) for each variant and for paired contrasts
experiments.seeds: v1 base seeds; inner splits base + 1000 + repeat. Deterministic
experiments.dissertation: Not in the dissertation. Closes the open item that only the reservoir code and PCA had been tuned.
caveats: Input is z-scored per epoch, as in the headline table, so that the comparison matches V2-01. See V2-05 for input without z-scoring.
PENDING: the run is queued behind the record regeneration; the record is added when it completes.

experiments.title: Per-epoch z-scoring artefact on ERP CORE
experiments.question: Does per-epoch z-scoring create above-chance decoding before stimulus onset on public data, and is the effect larger for a sustained component (P3) than a brief one (N170)?
data: ERP CORE N170 and P3 epoched single trials (public, doi:10.18115/D5JW4R; download into ./erpcore)
experiments.model: no reservoir: 28-channel scalp pattern in 15.6 ms bins under four normalizations
experiments.protocol: within participant: shrinkage LDA, stratified 5-fold repeated twice, fold-local standardization. Across participants: one average per participant and condition, 5 x 5 StratifiedGroupKFold, logistic regression
experiments.statistics: within: participant mean of pre-stimulus accuracy, one-sample t-test against 50% (primary test, fixed in the script). Two paradigms, uncorrected
experiments.seeds: within-participant splits seeded by participant id; across splits seed 0. Deterministic
experiments.dissertation: Not in the dissertation. Candidate methods paper.
caveats: The mechanism and prediction (MECHANISM.md) were committed at 69b6c97 before the results were seen.
Within participants the leak is small (at most 2 points) and not larger for P3; the prediction held fully only across participants.
The literature check was three web searches, not a systematic review.

experiments.title: Permutation null for across-participant pre-stimulus decoding
experiments.question: How high does pre-stimulus accuracy get by chance with 80 participant averages?
experiments.model: as ZS-01, across-participant regime
experiments.protocol: one participant-grouped 5-fold split, same splits for observed and null
experiments.statistics: each participant's two condition labels swapped with probability 1/2, 1000 permutations
experiments.metrics: mean balanced accuracy over pre-stimulus bins, permutation p
caveats: Covers the pre-stimulus mean, not individual bins. p = 0.001 is the floor.

experiments.title: Chapter 3: LIF reservoir characterization on synthetic input
experiments.question: How do leak, threshold and input structure shape the reservoir's operating point on a controlled synthetic task?
experiments.model: 33-input reservoir with the v1 update equations (not the one-input reservoir deployed on EEG)
experiments.protocol: StratifiedKFold(5); in experiments 4 and 6 the scaler is fitted on all trials before the split
caveats: No verifier and no manifest entry.
Its 'same as Chapter 4' task uses different noise and jitter from CH4-01.

experiments.title: Chapter 4: spike-to-embedding experiments on synthetic input
experiments.question: How do reservoir size, coding scheme, PCA dimension and operating point affect separability on a synthetic task?
experiments.model: 33-input reservoir, window 10 to 70 of 150 samples, BSC6, PCA
experiments.protocol: StratifiedKFold(5), fold-local scaler, but PCA is fitted on all trials before the split
experiments.statistics: accuracy mean and SD, Fisher discriminant ratio
experiments.seeds: 42 throughout; PCA unseeded in the runner
experiments.dissertation: Chapter 4 (dissertation/chLSMEmbeddings.tex). Writes 13 tracked PDFs in pictures/chLSMEmbeddings.
caveats: RUNNING THESE SCRIPTS OR THE VERIFIER IN PLACE OVERWRITES 13 TRACKED FIGURES. Use scripts/run_verifiers.py.
The Fisher ratio is inflated when features outnumber trials (review finding M5): pure noise at d=1536, n=400 gives 296.
The two scripts use different stimulus generators.
All 30 leak x threshold settings exceed 95% on this task (ceiling).

experiments.title: Chapter 5 legacy classification and graph propagation
experiments.question: Legacy: PCA-64 embeddings, random-weight graph propagation and baselines on the three-condition data.
experiments.model: N=256, beta=0.05, theta=0.5, dense uniform W_rec scaled to spectral radius 0.9, one scalar input per electrode; per-electrode seeds; PCA-64
experiments.protocol: StratifiedGroupKFold(10); PCA-64 fitted on all observations before the split; the GNN figure in reproduce_chapter5.py plots fixed values
experiments.dissertation: Chapter 5 archived tables (dissertation/chgraph.tex). Retained for provenance; superseded by CONF-01.
caveats: Not prospective performance: PCA is fitted on all observations before the split.

FIXED 2026-11 (D5), not rerun: reproduce_chapter5.py set its attention weights from held-out labels. On pure noise the old function scored 55% where chance is 33%. Accuracies taken from it before the fix are inflated.
The 'GNNs' are random-weight propagation, never trained.
results_manifest.json maps arch_pca64_svm and arch_gnn_sweep to run_chapter5_experiments.py, which has no SVM row, GIN or EdgeConv.
graph_diffusion_oversmoothing.py overwrites a tracked PDF in pictures/chGraphNeuralNetworks.
The '33% inter-channel variance at K=2' figure is hardcoded (190 to 99), not computed.

experiments.title: Experiment zero: subject-centering and the v1 reservoir definition
experiments.question: Legacy: effect of transductive subject-mean centering on three-condition accuracy. Also the file that defines the v1 LIF operator.
experiments.model: N=256, beta=0.05, theta=0.5, dense uniform W_rec scaled to spectral radius 0.9, one scalar input per electrode
experiments.protocol: StratifiedGroupKFold(10), LogisticRegression(C=0.1); per-electrode PCA and subject centering are fitted on all data first
caveats: FROZEN: this file's hash is part of the v1 confirmatory record and of every v2 record. LIFReservoir and bsc6_encode are imported by the confirmatory, novel and v2 code.
Its own loader keeps the pre-stimulus baseline (decimates all 1229 rows and keeps the first 256), unlike the confirmatory loader.
Subject centering uses the test participant's own data (transductive).

experiments.title: Chapter 5 baselines
experiments.question: Legacy: conventional and deep baselines on the three-condition data.
experiments.model: band power and Hjorth features with 8 sklearn classifiers; EEGNet, GRU and LSTM
experiments.protocol: sklearn: StratifiedGroupKFold(10), fold-local scaler, no global fit. PyTorch script: centering on all data, ungrouped validation split
caveats: The deep-baseline numbers in the dissertation table (72.0, 59.9, 58.0) come from the deprecated NumPy implementations, which train the output layer only.
canonical_pytorch_baselines.py cannot load the SHAPE text files as committed (its loader globs .mat).
No committed script writes baseline_deep_results.pkl.
results_manifest.json maps the Level-2 statistic rho = 7.2 to canonical_pytorch_baselines.py, which computes no variance decomposition.

experiments.title: Four-category extension of Chapter 5
experiments.question: Legacy: four-category classification, graph propagation variants and clinical screens.
experiments.model: one shared reservoir, samples 10 to 70, neuron-major BSC6, global PCA-64 (a different encoding from CONF-01 under the same name)
experiments.protocol: subject-level StratifiedKFold(10), RBF-SVC; PCA fitted on all data; graph adjacency chosen by best CV accuracy
experiments.statistics: Wilcoxon; clinical Mann-Whitney and Spearman at raw p < 0.05, no correction
caveats: Scripts read and write paths relative to the current directory and have no CLI.
Pre-stimulus samples are not removed and the sampling rate is marked 'assumed' 1000 Hz.
Its README states PCA is fitted per fold; the code fits it on all data.
results_manifest.json entry exp_4class_classification (centered 0.52, raw 0.404) is not produced by the listed script.

experiments.title: Chapter 6: echo-state and Lyapunov analysis
experiments.question: Legacy: does the reservoir converge from different initial states, and what is its driven Lyapunov exponent?
experiments.model: NOT the deployed reservoir: sparse Gaussian weights (10% density), no spectral scaling (radius about 0.26), reset without subtraction; full 1229-sample epoch including baseline
experiments.protocol: Benettin exponent with an initial separation of 1e-8
caveats: The echo-state evidence is from a different, weaker network than the one that produced the classification features. On the deployed network the property fails (V2-01).
A 1e-8 perturbation cannot flip a threshold, so the exponent measures leak and reset only.

experiments.title: Chapter 6: dynamical descriptor battery
experiments.question: Legacy: reliability, surrogate sensitivity, category dissociation, clinical interaction and temporal profile of spike-derived descriptors.
experiments.model: the sparse Chapter 6 reservoir (see CH6-01); descriptors include permutation entropy, Lempel-Ziv phrase count, relaxation and autocorrelation times
experiments.protocol: no cross-validation in the runners; reproduce_chapter6.py fits PCA(32) on all observations before StratifiedGroupKFold(5)
experiments.statistics: ICC(3,1), Wilcoxon, effect sizes; group-label permutation (500) in exp5; no multiple-comparison correction, no covariates
caveats: FIXED 2026-11 (D4), not rerun: the exp5 permutation p-value lacked the +1 term. Corrected values can only be larger, by at most 0.002.
'Seven metrics' means different sets in Chapter 6, Chapter 7 and the three-condition extension.
reproduce_chapter6.py claims ten experiments in its docstring and implements three.

experiments.title: Chapter 7: structure-function coupling kappa
experiments.question: Legacy: is the across-electrode coupling between dynamical descriptors and graph topology above an electrode-permutation null?
experiments.model: sparse Chapter 6 reservoir; theta-band phase-locking graph (fully weighted); C = 7 x 2 Spearman matrix across 34 electrodes; kappa = Frobenius norm of C over sqrt(14)
experiments.protocol: null: electrode rows permuted jointly; one-sided Wilcoxon over 844 observations treated as independent; Bonferroni over 14 cells
caveats: The electrode-permutation null assumes exchangeable electrodes. For two independent but spatially smooth fields the review measured a 90% false-positive rate. A valid null needs electrode coordinates.
The committed pickle holds 2000 permutations per observation; the script and the manifest say 5000.
Includes participant 195 (844 observations), whom the corrected analysis excludes (840).
The result files are keyed by real participant ID (docs/REPOSITORY_AUDIT.md, finding S1).

FIXED 2026-11 (D3), not rerun: clustering was twice the Onnela coefficient. No statistic changes (coupling and kappa are rank-based); stored clustering values are 2x. The figure directory is now ARSPI_FIGURE_DIR.

experiments.title: Chapter 7: variance partition and category contrasts of kappa
experiments.question: Legacy: how much of kappa is between-subject, and do coupling matrices differ between categories?
data: committed chapter7_results CSV files (derived from restricted data)
experiments.model: as CH7-01
experiments.protocol: within-subject label permutation (5000); cellwise Wilcoxon with Bonferroni 14; sign-flip Frobenius test (5000)
experiments.dissertation: Chapter 7. kappa has near-zero reliability across categories (ICC 0.059).
caveats: RUNNING B OR THE VERIFIER IN PLACE OVERWRITES ch7_expB_results.npz AND 7 TRACKED PDFs in pictures/chSynthesis. Use scripts/run_verifiers.py.
The committed npz was written by an earlier version of experiment B; its keys do not match the current script.

experiments.title: Chapter 7: clinical associations of coupling
experiments.question: Legacy: does kappa differ by diagnosis, and do coupling features add to classification of diagnosis?
experiments.model: subject-mean kappa; feature sets T, D, T+D, T+D+kappa
experiments.protocol: StratifiedKFold(5) x 10 repeats over participants, scaler in-fold, logistic regression
experiments.statistics: Mann-Whitney for 5 diagnoses with Bonferroni 5; interaction permutation uncorrected; Wilcoxon over 50 dependent folds
experiments.dissertation: Chapter 7 clinical section. Cohort-level and hypothesis-generating by the dissertation's own scope statement.
caveats: REPLAYED 2026-11-21: both scripts rerun on the committed tables and the SCID-5 spreadsheet reproduce the dissertation's values (experiment D: p from 0.32 to 0.92; experiment E: best AUC 0.622). FIXED (D9): conclusions are now computed from the run instead of printed as fixed text.
No script in the repository writes subject_features.csv or observation_features.csv.
No age, sex or medication covariates. v2's corrected depression family (V2-03) found nothing.

experiments.title: Three-condition extension of Chapters 6 and 7
experiments.question: Do the descriptor and coupling analyses carry over to the three-condition stream?
experiments.model: dense Gaussian W_rec scaled to 0.9 (a third reservoir definition); baseline removed, decimated, z-scored
experiments.protocol: Friedman, Wilcoxon, Mann-Whitney by diagnosis, medication and sex; SVC and logistic regression with StratifiedGroupKFold
experiments.statistics: group-level kappa null (5000); no multiple-comparison correction anywhere
caveats: Scripts 02 to 04 execute at import and read paths relative to the current directory.
Several metrics share names with Chapter 6 but are defined differently.
The manifest describes a 'median across 211 subject-averaged kappa' and a Wilcoxon test that the script does not compute.
FIXED 2026-11, not rerun: permutation p-values now use the +1 form (D4); the Fano bound includes its K-1 term (D6); a variance share is no longer labelled ICC(3,1) (D7).

experiments.title: Layer ablation
experiments.question: Legacy: which feature blocks carry the emotion and the clinical signal?
data: shape_features_211.pkl and ch6_ch7_3class_features.pkl (derived from restricted data)
experiments.model: feature blocks from Chapters 5 to 7
experiments.protocol: StratifiedGroupKFold(10) single repeat, fold-local scaler, class-weighted logistic regression
caveats: CANNOT BE REGENERATED: no script in the repository writes shape_features_211.pkl.
Some result values are hardcoded strings in the script.
The verifier re-implements the logic inline and never imports the script.
Uses a LogisticRegression keyword that recent scikit-learn may reject (not executed here).

experiments.title: Interpretability Level 1 and Level 3 statistics
experiments.question: How well do reservoir outputs track the late positive potential?
data: a pickle with key raw_eeg or X_raw (derived from restricted data; no script in the repository writes it)
experiments.model: N=256, beta=0.05, theta=0.5, dense uniform W_rec scaled to spectral radius 0.9, one scalar input per electrode; Level 1 uses one shared reservoir and a 34-input reservoir; Level 3 per-electrode seeds
experiments.protocol: Level 1: median signed Pearson r between LPP mean and BSC bins; RidgeCV with GroupKFold(10)
experiments.dissertation: Interpretability audit table: pre-reservoir r = 0.82, post-reservoir absolute r = 0.23.
caveats: The 0.82 value is not computed by either script; in Level 3 it is a printed literal. It correlates two windows of raw z-scored EEG, never touches the reservoir, and its sign is negative. v2 recommends withdrawing it.
No verifier, no CI step, no results file.
The Level 3 docstring says seven descriptors; the code computes six.

experiments.title: EEGNet saliency comparison and attention prototype
experiments.question: Exploratory comparisons of where a trained EEGNet and an attention readout place weight in time.
experiments.model: EEGNet; attention readout over six BSC bins
experiments.protocol: saliency: trained on all data, no split. Attention: StratifiedGroupKFold(10)
caveats: FIXED 2026-11 (D2), not rerun: the saliency script fed the network time as channels. The 402 to 691 ms peaks reported from it are unsupported until it is rerun.
The file named run_arspinet_v2_attention_prototype.py predates and is unrelated to the arspinet_v2 package.
Needs PyTorch, which CI never installs.

experiments.title: Compression study: SRP against PCA, reservoir instrument, necessity map
experiments.question: N1: does a data-independent projection beat fold-local PCA? N2: is the reservoir a stable instrument? N3: which structure in the code is necessary?
experiments.model: v1 confirmatory chain; fold-local blockwise PCA
experiments.protocol: v1 confirmatory splits
experiments.seeds: SRP seeds 1000 to 1009 in fast mode
caveats: N1 (SRP +4.4 pp over PCA) IS SUPERSEDED: with PCA left unwhitened and C tuned the advantage disappears (V2-04).
The committed JSON files carry no provenance, a hand-added note field, and interpretation strings that NOVEL_RESULTS.md retracts. experiments/novel/README.md is stale against both results files.
Numbers come from a --fast run.

experiments.title: Nuisance-alignment study
experiments.question: Is PCA's loss explained by alignment of its leading components with the subject subspace?
data: synthetic generators for M1a, M1b, M3
experiments.model: principal angles between PCA and subject subspaces; subject-to-condition variance ratio
experiments.protocol: geometry fitted on the full matrix by design (descriptive)
caveats: Its own results file states: 'We therefore do not claim M2 explains the N1 accuracy gap.'
The variance ratio has no noise floor (pure noise gives a large value). Use arspinet_v2.nuisance instead.
M1b and M3 are not in results_manifest.json.

experiments.title: External replication on TCRZEM
experiments.question: Does the SRP-over-PCA difference appear on an independent affective-picture ERP dataset?
experiments.model: v1 confirmatory chain on 228 participants, 41 channels
experiments.protocol: v1 confirmatory splits; full epoch resampled to 256 samples with no pre-stimulus removal
caveats: Absolute accuracy is near chance (45.5% for three classes).
Inherits the standardized-PCA handicap that V2-04 identified; not rerun with tuned PCA.
No verifier exercises the loader.
No provenance block.

experiments.title: Defense experiments A to D and theoretical-bounds figure
experiments.question: Supplementary analyses prepared for the defense: driven Lyapunov exponent, embedding dimension, memory capacity, channel-permutation control.
data: a 633-trial pickle with keys X_ds, y, subjects (derived from restricted data; the committed writer of that filename does not produce these keys)
experiments.model: A uses the sparse Chapter 6 reservoir; C uses the v1 reservoir with the leak swept; B and D define none
experiments.protocol: D: one-vs-rest logistic regression, 5-fold StratifiedGroupKFold, 500 permutations of a per-trial channel shuffle
experiments.metrics: lambda_1, embedding dimension, memory capacity, AUC
experiments.dissertation: Defense deck (ARSPI-Net_Defense.tex) only. No output appears in the dissertation chapters.
caveats: FIXED 2026-11 (D1), regenerated: experiment C computed its fading-memory time constant on membranes. The unfixed script reproduced the committed CSV byte for byte; after the fix only that column changes, and it remains uninformative (7 of 20 infinite).
FIXED 2026-11 (D4), not rerun: experiment D's permutation p-value lacked the +1 term; its committed CSV shows 0.000000 where the corrected value is 0.002.
Theoretical-bounds figure: measured lambda_1 lies above its 'upper bound' and measured dimension below its 'lower bound' (review finding M4).
The A and B data files are keyed by real participant ID.
No verifier covers this directory. build_deck.py needs PyMuPDF, which is declared nowhere.

experiments.title: Reservoir animations
experiments.question: Animated illustrations of reservoir dynamics for talks.
data: shape_features_211.pkl (derived from restricted data; optional for some animations)
experiments.model: v1 reservoir; one animation uses the sparse Chapter 6 reservoir
experiments.protocol: none
experiments.dissertation: Not in the dissertation. Outputs under pictures/animations.
caveats: Without --pkl one animation falls back to synthetic data and overwrites a tracked real-data animation.
Needs ffmpeg and pillow, declared nowhere.
